teaser: Why do giraffes have such long necks?
fact: A giraffe's neck can be up to 6 feet (2 meters) long — that's as tall as a grown-up! They use their long necks to reach tasty leaves at the very top of trees.
Nope! Elephants are the only animals that can't jump. Even though they are super strong, their heavy bodies just don't bounce like that!

teaser: How big is a blue whale's heart?
fact: A blue whale's heart is as big as a small car! It only beats about 8 to 10 times every minute — that's really slow.

teaser: How many brains does an octopus have?
fact: An octopus has NINE brains! One main brain in its head, and a mini brain in each of its eight arms.
Koalas have fingerprints that are almost exactly like human fingerprints! Even scientists can hardly tell them apart.
Butterflies taste with their FEET! They land on a flower and know right away if it tastes yummy.

teaser: Why does the arctic fox change color?
fact: An arctic fox's fur turns white in winter to hide in the snow, and brown in summer to blend in with the rocks and grass.

teaser: How many teeth does a snail have?
fact: A garden snail has about 14,000 tiny teeth on its tongue! They're so small you can't even see them.
Saturn is so light and fluffy that it would float in a giant bathtub of water! It is mostly made of gas, so it's lighter than water.
Yes! The sun is a giant star in the middle of our solar system. It's so big that about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it.

teaser: Is the Moon moving away from Earth?
fact: The Moon drifts about 1.5 inches (4 cm) farther from Earth every single year — that's about as fast as your fingernails grow!

teaser: Do footprints stay on the Moon?
fact: There's no wind or rain on the Moon, so the astronauts' footprints from 1969 are still there — they could stay for millions of years!
'Shooting stars' aren't stars at all — they are tiny bits of rock and dust burning up as they zoom through Earth's sky!
Yes! Space is totally silent because sound needs air to travel, and there is no air in space.
A T-Rex had teeth as big as bananas — up to 9 inches (23 cm) long! And when one fell out, a new one grew in its place.
Yes! Birds are living dinosaurs. Scientists say chickens are the closest living relatives of the mighty T-Rex!
Dinosaur eggs weren't that big — the biggest ones were about the size of a soccer ball, even though the dinos themselves were huge!

teaser: How small was a Stegosaurus brain?
fact: A Stegosaurus was as big as a bus, but its brain was only about the size of a walnut!
About 66 million years ago, a giant asteroid crashed into Earth. It kicked up dust that blocked the sun and cooled the planet, wiping out the dinosaurs.

teaser: How many teeth do sharks have?
fact: Sharks can grow and lose thousands of teeth in their lifetime — some lose a tooth every single week, but new ones keep growing!
There's a tiny jellyfish that can grow old and then turn back into a baby again — making it effectively immortal!

teaser: What's the loudest animal in the ocean?
fact: The sperm whale makes a clicking sound louder than a jet engine! It's the loudest sound made by any animal on Earth.
When scared, a pufferfish gulps water and blows up like a balloon to look bigger — and it's covered in spines to keep predators away!
Crabs have legs that bend in special joints, so it's much easier for them to scuttle sideways than to walk forwards!
Penguins can't fly in the air, but they are amazing 'flyers' underwater! They swim so fast it looks like they're flying through the sea.
Emperor penguins are the tallest penguins — they can grow about 4 feet (1.2 m) tall, about as tall as a 7-year-old!

teaser: Why do penguins look like they're wearing tuxedos?
fact: A penguin's black-and-white colors are camouflage! The black blends with the dark ocean from above, and the white blends with the ice from below.

teaser: Do penguins slide on their bellies?
fact: Yes! Penguins toboggan — they slide on their bellies across the ice because it's much faster and easier than waddling.
Emperor penguins huddle together in huge groups, taking turns standing in the warm middle. They can be thousands strong!

teaser: How do bees talk to each other?
fact: Honeybees do a special 'waggle dance' to tell their friends exactly where to find yummy flowers!
Spider silk is stronger than steel of the same weight! A web as thick as a pencil could stop a jumbo jet.
Ants can carry things 50 times their own body weight — that's like a kid lifting a whole car!
A mosquito flaps its tiny wings up to 600 times every second — that fast flapping is what makes the buzzing sound!

teaser: How many legs do insects have?
fact: All insects have exactly six legs — spiders are NOT insects because they have eight legs!
Parrots can learn to copy human words. The cleverest, Alex the parrot, knew over 100 words and could even count!

teaser: Can owls turn their heads all the way around?
fact: Owls can't spin 360°, but they CAN turn their heads 270° — almost all the way around — to look behind them!
The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth! It can dive at over 240 mph (390 km/h).
Yes! Penguins are birds that can't fly. They have feathers, lay eggs, and are fantastic swimmers.
A hummingbird's wings can flap up to 80 times every second — so fast they look like a blur!
Everything around you — even you! — is made of tiny building blocks called atoms. They're so small that billions could fit on the head of a pin.
A lightning bolt is about 5 times hotter than the surface of the sun — around 54,000°F (30,000°C)!

teaser: Why do magnets stick to things?
fact: Magnets have an invisible force called magnetism that pulls some metals toward them — the same force that keeps compass needles pointing north!
Rainbows happen when sunlight passes through raindrops and splits into all the colors — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet!

teaser: How much of Earth is water?
fact: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered in water — but only a tiny bit of it is fresh water that we can drink.
Honey can last for thousands of years without going bad! Archaeologists found 3,000-year-old honey that was still yummy.
People have been eating popcorn for over 5,000 years! Ancient people popped corn over open fires.

teaser: Do carrots help you see better?
fact: Carrots are full of vitamin A, which helps keep your eyes healthy — but they won't give you super night vision!
Surprise! By science rules, bananas ARE berries — but strawberries and raspberries are not! Scientists group berries by how they grow.
Yes! Apples float because about 25% of their volume is air — that's also why they bob in a bowl of water.
Earth spins at about 1,000 mph (1,600 km/h) at the equator — but you don't feel it because everything moves together!
The Eiffel Tower can grow about 6 inches taller in summer! The metal expands when it gets hot.

teaser: Can you see the Great Wall from space?
fact: You actually can't see the Great Wall of China from space with your eyes — it's too thin! That's a fun myth.

teaser: How many volcanoes are erupting right now?
fact: There are about 1,500 active volcanoes on Earth, and about 20 of them are erupting at any moment!
Antarctica is a desert! It's the driest, windiest, and coldest continent — and it holds most of Earth's fresh water as ice.
Soccer (football) is the most popular sport in the world — more than 3.5 billion fans play or watch it!
The first Olympic Games were held in Ancient Greece over 2,700 years ago!

teaser: Why are basketball hoops 10 feet high?
fact: Basketball hoops are 10 feet (3 m) high because that's the height of the gym balcony where the sport was invented!

teaser: Are gold medals really made of gold?
fact: Olympic gold medals are mostly silver with a thin layer of gold on top — but they are still super special!
The word 'robot' came from a play in 1920! The first working robot in a factory was used in 1961.

teaser: How big were the first computers?
fact: The first electronic computers filled entire rooms! The famous ENIAC computer weighed about 27 tons.

teaser: Are there more phones than people?
fact: Yes! There are more mobile phones in the world than there are people on Earth.
The internet started as a project in 1969 called ARPANET — it was built to connect just a few university computers.

teaser: What do pandas eat all day?
fact: Pandas spend up to 12 hours a day eating bamboo — they munch on up to 30 kg (66 lbs) of it every single day!

teaser: How loud is a lion's roar?
fact: A lion's roar can be heard from 5 miles (8 km) away — it's the loudest roar of all the big cats!

teaser: Are zebras black with white stripes?
fact: Zebras are actually black with white stripes! Each zebra has its own unique stripe pattern, just like human fingerprints.

teaser: How many spines does a hedgehog have?
fact: A hedgehog has about 5,000 to 7,000 spines on its back! Each one is a stiff, hollow hair that lies flat until danger appears.
A camel's hump stores fat, not water! That fat gives camels energy when there's no food to find in the desert.

teaser: How do geckos stick to walls?
fact: Geckos have millions of tiny hairs on their feet that use a special force to stick to walls and even ceilings!

teaser: What's the tallest volcano in the solar system?
fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system — almost 3 times taller than Mount Everest!

teaser: What is Jupiter's Great Red Spot?
fact: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been raging for over 350 years — it's so big that Earth could fit inside it!

teaser: How much does a spacesuit weigh?
fact: A spacesuit weighs about 280 pounds (127 kg) on Earth, but in space it feels almost weightless!
A comet's tail always points away from the sun! The sun's heat and wind blow the dust and gas back as the comet zooms along.

teaser: How many stars are in the Milky Way?
fact: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, has between 100 and 400 billion stars — that's more stars than grains of sand on a beach!
Diplodocus could grow over 90 feet (27 m) long — longer than three buses parked end to end!

teaser: Why were T-Rex arms so small?
fact: Nobody knows for sure, but T-Rex's tiny arms were probably for holding prey close or helping it get back up from the ground!

teaser: Did dinosaurs take care of their babies?
fact: Yes! Some dinosaurs built nests and watched over their eggs, just like birds do today.
The ostrich-like dinosaur Ornithomimus could run about 40 mph (64 km/h) — about as fast as a racehorse!

teaser: How big was a baby T-Rex?
fact: A baby T-Rex hatched from an egg about the size of a grapefruit and weighed about as much as a small dog!
Fish don't sleep like we do, but they rest! Many find a safe spot and slow way down to save energy.

teaser: How big is a giant squid?
fact: A giant squid can grow longer than a school bus — up to 43 feet (13 m) long! Its eyes are as big as dinner plates.
The Japanese spider crab has legs that can stretch up to 12 feet (3.8 m) across — wider than any other animal!
Dolphins rest half their brain at a time so they can keep swimming and breathing while they sleep!
Clownfish live inside stinging sea anemones! The tentacles protect them from enemies, and they keep the anemone clean.
Penguins can swim up to 22 mph (36 km/h) — faster than an Olympic swimmer!

teaser: Who keeps the penguin egg warm?
fact: The daddy emperor penguin keeps the egg warm on his feet under a flap of skin for two whole months while mum goes to find food!

teaser: Do penguins jump out of the water?
fact: Yes! Penguins leap out of the water like little rockets to land safely on the ice or escape from enemies.

teaser: Do all penguins live where it's cold?
fact: Not all! Galápagos penguins live near the equator where it's warm and sunny — the only penguins that live in warm places.
Male crickets chirp by rubbing their wings together to attract female crickets — they can chirp hundreds of times a minute!

teaser: How does a caterpillar become a butterfly?
fact: Inside its chrysalis, a caterpillar melts into goo and rebuilds its whole body — and comes out as a beautiful butterfly!
Some ants are farmers! Leafcutter ants grow their own fungus gardens, and some even keep tiny 'cows' called aphids.

teaser: How much honey does a bee make?
fact: A single honeybee makes only about 1/12 of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life — it takes thousands of bees to fill a jar!

teaser: How far do monarch butterflies travel?
fact: Monarch butterflies migrate up to 3,000 miles (4,800 km) — some fly for months to reach warm places!

teaser: Do birds really fly south for winter?
fact: Many birds migrate! Some travel thousands of miles to find food and warmer weather when winter comes.
Ostriches can't fly, but they are the fastest running birds — they can sprint at 45 mph (70 km/h)!
Ducks have special oil on their feathers that makes water roll right off — they're naturally waterproof!
Some parrots can live 80 years or more — a parrot can be your friend for your whole life!
Sound travels about 767 mph (1,235 km/h) through air — faster than a jet plane!
Astronauts float because they are falling around Earth at the same speed as their spaceship — it's called free fall!

teaser: Are two snowflakes ever the same?
fact: Snowflakes form in so many different ways that scientists believe no two snowflakes are exactly alike!

teaser: Where does the sun's energy come from?
fact: The sun shines because of a huge reaction called fusion — it squishes hydrogen atoms together to make helium and release light and heat!

teaser: Why does your hair stand up?
fact: When you rub a balloon on your hair, tiny electric charges build up and make your hair stand on end!
Potatoes are actually roots, not vegetables! And a potato can grow a whole new plant from just one 'eye' on its skin.
The fruit came first! The color 'orange' was actually named after the fruit, not the other way around.

teaser: Why does Swiss cheese have holes?
fact: The holes in Swiss cheese are made by tiny gas bubbles from special bacteria during the cheese-making!
Peanuts aren't nuts at all — they are legumes, related to beans and peas, and they grow underground!

teaser: Why do lemons make you pucker?
fact: Lemons are full of a sour acid called citric acid — it makes your mouth pucker when it touches your taste buds!
There are more than 900,000 islands in the world's oceans — but only about 11,000 are big enough for people to live on!
Mount Everest is about 5.5 miles (8.8 km) tall — high enough that you can see the curve of the Earth from the top!
The Nile in Africa is the longest river — about 4,130 miles (6,650 km) long, running through 11 countries!
The Sahara is the biggest hot desert — it's about the size of the whole United States!

teaser: Why do we have time zones?
fact: Earth is round and spins, so different parts see the sun at different times — that's why we have 24 time zones!
Sailfish are the fastest swimmers in the ocean — they can zip along at 68 mph (110 km/h)!

teaser: How often is the World Cup?
fact: The soccer World Cup happens every 4 years, and billions of people around the world tune in to watch it!

teaser: How many stitches are on a baseball?
fact: A baseball has exactly 108 double stitches on its cover!
A marathon is 26.2 miles (42 km) long — that's the distance from the town of Marathon in ancient Greece to the city of Athens!

teaser: How long do the Olympics last?
fact: The modern Summer Olympics last about 16 days and host thousands of athletes from almost every country on Earth!

teaser: Why aren't keyboard keys in ABC order?
fact: The QWERTY keyboard was designed over 140 years ago to keep the typewriter's hammers from jamming — and we still use it today!
Before USB sticks, people saved their files on floppy disks — the earliest ones could only hold about as much as a small photo!

teaser: What was the first video game?
fact: A game called 'Pong', made in 1972, was one of the first video games people could play at home!
Wi-Fi sends information through invisible radio waves — like a very fast, silent conversation between your device and the router!
Computers understand everything as tiny switches that are either ON (1) or OFF (0) — that's called binary code!
